concepts.name: Radian measure
concepts.learningObjective: The student can locate an angle in radians on the unit circle and convert between degrees and radians.
concepts.primer: Angles measured by arc length on the unit circle; one full turn is 2π.
keyFacts: π radians is half a revolution, or 180°.
pitfalls: π radians is half a circle; a full circle is 2π.

concepts.name: Period of sin(bx) and cos(bx)
concepts.learningObjective: The student can compute the period of y = sin(bx) or cos(bx) and explain why a larger b shortens it.
concepts.primer: The horizontal length of one full cycle, 2π/|b|.
keyFacts: The period of y = sin(bx) is 2π/|b|.
Increasing b makes the graph repeat more often.
pitfalls: A bigger b squeezes the wave, so sin(2x) has period π.

concepts.name: Amplitude
concepts.learningObjective: The student can read the amplitude from an equation or graph and distinguish it from the peak-to-trough distance.
concepts.primer: |A| in y = A·sin(x): the height of the wave above its midline.
keyFacts: The amplitude of y = A sin x is |A|.
Changing A does not change the period.
pitfalls: Peak-to-trough is twice the amplitude; amplitude is |A|.

concepts.name: Solving sin(x) = k on [0, 2π)
concepts.learningObjective: The student can find every solution of a basic sine equation on one period.
concepts.primer: Isolate the sine, find the reference angle, then use the quadrants where sine has that sign.
keyFacts: Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.
pitfalls: It has two: π/6 in quadrant I and 5π/6 in quadrant II.

title: The Sky Clock

theme.setting: An old observatory tower with a broken sky clock

premise: The astronomer's star chart is at the top of a broken sky clock. Fix each machine as you climb to reach it.

encounters.targetMisconception: π radians is a full circle.
encounters.prompt: This line is one full turn of a circle, laid out flat from 0 to 2π. Step onto 5π/6.
hints: Find π first. The line ends at 2π, so π is only halfway along.
5π/6 is five sixths of π. Split the part from 0 to π into six equal steps.
It's past the π/2 mark and short of π, closer to π.
encounters.wrongFeedback: Not there. π sits halfway along the line, so count sixths of π from 0.
encounters.debriefLine: Radians measure how far you go around a circle. 5π/6 is 5/12 of one full turn.

sourceRef.quote: An angle of π radians corresponds to half a revolution.

encounters.targetMisconception: sin(2x) has period 4π, twice as long as sin(x).
encounters.prompt: The door's rings spin on y = sin(2t). Set the dial to one period, the time for one full turn.
hints: Look at the 2 inside sin(2t). It makes these rings spin faster than plain sin(t).
One period is 2π divided by the number next to t. Here that's 2π ÷ 2.
Plain sin(t) takes 2π. Twice as fast means half of 2π.
encounters.wrongFeedback: The 2 makes the rings spin faster. So one turn takes less time than 2π.
encounters.debriefLine: The period of y = sin(2t) is π. That's 2π divided by 2, the number next to t.

sourceRef.quote: The period of y = sin(bx) is 2π/|b|.

encounters.targetMisconception: Amplitude is the distance from peak to trough.
encounters.prompt: Three chests make claims about amplitude, how high a wave goes above its middle. Point your lantern at the one that's lying.

statements.explanation: Amplitude is the size of the number in front. Here that's 3.

statements.text: The amplitude of y = 3sin(x) is 6, from top to bottom
statements.explanation: Top to bottom is 6, but that's twice the amplitude. The amplitude is 3.

statements.text: Multiplying sin(x) by 3 doesn't change its period
statements.explanation: The 3 makes the wave taller. Only the number next to x changes the period.

hints: Two claims give a different amplitude for 3sin(x). They can't both be right.
Amplitude goes from the middle line up to the top. For 3sin(x), the top is at 3.
The claim about the period is true. Compare the other two.
encounters.wrongFeedback: That one's true. Look for the claim that measures the whole swing.
encounters.debriefLine: The mimic said "The amplitude of y = 3sin(x) is 6, from top to bottom". But amplitude only goes from the middle to the top, so it's 3.

sourceRef.quote: The amplitude of y = A sin x is |A|.

encounters.targetMisconception: sin(x) = 1/2 has only one solution on [0, 2π).
encounters.prompt: Put the planks in order to solve 2sin(x) = 1 for x between 0 and 2π. One plank doesn't belong.

steps: Get sin(x) by itself, so sin(x) = 1/2
Sine is positive in the top half, quadrants I and II
Write both answers, x = π/6 and x = 5π/6
decoys: Take the inverse sine of 2 first

hints: The 2 in 2sin(x) is in the way. Get rid of it before you look for any angle.
Once sin(x) = 1/2, find the smallest angle with that sine. Then check where else sine is positive.
The inverse sine of 2 plank doesn't fit. No angle has a sine of 2.
encounters.wrongFeedback: That order doesn't work. You can't find the angle until sin(x) is by itself.
encounters.debriefLine: You solved 2sin(x) = 1 in 4 steps. Sine is positive twice around the circle, so there were two answers.

sourceRef.quote: To solve a trigonometric equation, first isolate the trigonometric function.

encounters.targetMisconception: sin(2x) has period 4π, twice as long as sin(x).
encounters.prompt: Three chests make claims about periods, and one is lying. Point your lantern at it.

statements.text: y = sin(2x) repeats every π, twice as often as sin(x)
y = sin(2x) has period 4π, twice as long as sin(x)
statements.explanation: The 2 makes the wave faster, so the period shrinks to π.

statements.text: y = cos(x/2) has period 4π, twice as long as cos(x)

hints: Two chests give sin(2x) different periods. The 2 makes that wave go faster.
Period is 2π divided by the number next to x. For sin(2x), that's 2π ÷ 2.
The chest about cos(x/2) is telling the truth. Compare the other two.
encounters.wrongFeedback: That chest is telling the truth. Check each claim by dividing 2π by the number next to x.
encounters.debriefLine: The mimic said "y = sin(2x) has period 4π, twice as long as sin(x)". But a bigger number next to x makes the period shorter.

sourceRef.quote: Larger values of b compress the graph horizontally.

encounters.prompt: The Warden's shield swings on y = 3sin((π/2)t). Match its period, the time for one full swing, to get past.
hints: The 3 in front only makes the shield swing wider. It doesn't change the timing.
Period is 2π divided by the number next to t. Here that's 2π ÷ (π/2).
Dividing by π/2 is the same as multiplying by 2/π. The π's cancel, leaving 2 × 2.
encounters.wrongFeedback: The 3 makes it swing wider. The timing comes from the π/2 next to t.
encounters.debriefLine: The shield's amplitude was 3 and its period was 4. Only the π/2 next to t set the period.

sourceRef.quote: The value of A stretches the graph vertically but leaves the period unchanged.

intro.text: The star chart is at the top. Fix each machine, and we can climb.

outro.text: You got the star chart. Every machine on the way up is moving again.

beats.text: Those rings spin on a sine wave. Watch how fast they turn.
Nobody gets past me with the wrong timing.
Your timing matches mine. You may pass.

pre.prompt: What is the period of y = sin(3x)?
What is the amplitude of y = -4cos(x)?

post.prompt: What is the period of y = cos(x/3)?
Which equation swings twice as high as y = sin(x)?
Which angle is a quarter turn?
